year_level_findings: 1935 is the first year in this corpus where publication cadence itself becomes a design variable through the 11-12 combined issue.
The year repeatedly treats production artefacts and demonstration inserts as editorial objects rather than peripheral advertising.
Photography, typography, public printing, commercial graphics and ordinary information increasingly occupy the same critical field.
Editorial identity survives personnel change, printer change, delayed production, page-count reduction and combined numbering; therefore identity cannot be reduced to a fixed visual template.
Doré should learn issue architecture under constraint: fewer pages, changed cadence, foreign objects and special-purpose issues must each trigger a fresh composition rather than template compression.
dore_judge_rules: CADENCE_IS_DESIGN: publication timing and combined numbering may legitimately change sequence grammar.
CONSTRAINT_GENERATES_HIERARCHY: fewer pages should intensify editorial choices instead of shrinking an existing layout.
FOREIGN_OBJECTS_KEEP_LOCAL_GRAMMAR: inserted specimens may preserve their own visual identity.
IDENTITY_ABOVE_SURFACE: a publication remains itself across designers, printers and issue-specific visual systems.
SOURCE_CONFLICTS_STAY_VISIBLE: contradictory archive metadata must be flagged, not silently harmonized.
TECHNIQUE_IS_CONTENT_WHEN_SEMANTIC: reproduction, ink, paper and type technologies may become editorial meaning when the subject warrants it.
